name: 7 Hz sine at 1-20 ms point durations, right hemisphere (Booth 2003)
origin: Booth, Koren & Persinger (Laurentian University), 2003 point-duration study, n = 6
summary: Booth, Koren & Persinger's (2003) test of point ('pixel') duration alone: a 7 Hz sine over the right hemisphere, played with points of 1, 3, 5, 7, 10 and 20 ms for 5 min each. In six subjects the paper prints the highest rates of left-sided sensed presences (23 and 28 %) and of occipital EEG spikes (21 and 31 %) at 1 and 10 ms; only some of the differences were tested.
notes: The paper applied 7 Hz sine waves with point durations of 1, 3, 5, 7, 10 or 20 ms for 5 min each, in a sequential counterbalanced order, to six subjects, over the right hemisphere through solenoids in a helmet (Booth 2003 pp.1-2 [951-952]). This program plays the same frequency, point durations and block length on three right-side coils (T8, TP8, P8: this project's reading), all on together, with the left side silent. The paper does not say whether the helmet's usual 0.5-s switching between its four solenoid pairs ran (p.2 [952]). The lab later described these fields as more intense over the right hemisphere than the left (St-Pierre 2006 p.10 [1088]), so in the original the left side was weaker, not off. The lab's six number columns are not published. A 142.9-ms period is not a whole number of 7-ms or 20-ms points, so the lab's files and this sample-and-hold sine can differ in detail. The six orders are not published either: this file uses one row of a balanced Latin square (1, 3, 20, 5, 10, 7 ms). For repeat sessions reorder the phases to another row: 3 5 1 7 20 10; 5 7 3 10 1 20; 7 10 5 20 3 1; 10 20 7 1 5 3; 20 1 10 3 7 5. Field: the paper set 1 uT by adjusting the amplifier in the software and does not say where it was measured (p.1 [951]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. Support: six subjects, one lab, not repeated. Left-side presences were 23, 9, 15, 13, 28 and 12 % for 1, 3, 5, 7, 10 and 20 ms, and the only tests reported are 1 ms above 3 ms and above 20 ms; spikes were 21, 12, 10, 6, 31 and 19 %, with 1 and 10 ms above 7 ms (p.2 [952]). Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices or pregnancy; stop on fear or distress.
setting: Seated in a quiet, dark room with the eyes covered; in the original, EEG was recorded over the occipital regions and presences were scored by side.
schedule: One session per person in the original. For a self-test, use a different Latin-square order each time and compare with sham sessions (the app's Blind option).
source: Booth, Koren & Persinger 2003, Increased proportions of sensed presences and occipital spikes with 1- and 10-msec. point duration of continuous 7-Hz transcerebral magnetic fields, Percept Mot Skills 97:951-952 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14738362/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
